subject.title: fix(memory): stop deep promotion from growing MEMORY.md

question: Should memory-core adopt archive-first promotion as the permanent storage model, and if so must the existing `memoryFileMaxChars` contract continue to bound archive retention or be explicitly migrated and retired?
rationale: The code can implement several valid policies, but automation cannot decide whether OpenClaw should retain all promoted history, preserve an existing operator safety setting, or continue the shipped bounded-root model.

options.title: Archive with an explicit budget
options.body: Adopt archive-first storage, define bounded retention or equivalent cleanup semantics, and migrate the existing setting through the plugin-owned doctor path before merge.

options.title: Accept unbounded archives
options.body: Intentionally retain all promotion history, remove or migrate the obsolete setting with a visible warning, and explicitly accept the indexing, disk, backup, and sensitive-data consequences.

options.title: Keep bounded root compaction
options.body: Do not adopt the new storage model and retain the shipped compaction behavior, potentially improving summaries or pointers in a narrower follow-up.

recommendation.title: Archive with an explicit budget
recommendation.body: Adopt archive-first storage, define bounded retention or equivalent cleanup semantics, and migrate the existing setting through the plugin-owned doctor path before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The original promotion-pipeline history gives this contributor the strongest connection to the permanent storage and upgrade semantics.
